edibilityNotes: Toxic. Causes gastrointestinal illness (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea), sometimes with delayed onset, associated with fasciculol-type triterpene compounds. The flesh is also intensely and persistently bitter, which usually deters consumption. Not a food species under any preparation. Its habit of growing in dense clusters on wood alongside genuinely edible species (and the deadly Galerina marginata) makes misidentification a real risk.
description: Sulphur Tuft (Hypholoma fasciculare) is a common, widespread wood-rotting mushroom that fruits in dense, crowded clusters on dead hardwood and conifer stumps, logs, and buried roots. Caps are typically 2–6 cm across, convex to flattened, sulphur-yellow to greenish-yellow and often more orange-brown or tan toward the centre. The crowded gills start sulphur-yellow, become distinctly green to olive-tinged with age, and finally turn purple-brown as the spores mature. The slender yellowish stems are often rusty-stained below and frequently fused at the base in the cluster; a faint fibrillose ring zone may be present from the cortina-like partial veil. The spore print is purple-brown. The flesh is yellow and intensely bitter. It is a saprotroph, fruiting from spring through autumn (mainly late summer to late autumn) and sometimes in mild winters, and is one of the most frequently encountered cluster-forming wood mushrooms in temperate woodlands. It is toxic and not edible.
distribution: Cosmopolitan and very common across temperate regions, including Europe, North America, Asia, and Australasia.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Hypholoma capnoides
dangerousLookalikes.note: Edible. Grows on conifer wood; gills are greyish to smoky-grey (never green-tinged) before turning purple-brown, and the flesh is mild rather than bitter.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Hypholoma lateritium
dangerousLookalikes.note: Brick Cap. Reputedly edible (cook; some sources caution), clusters on hardwood; cap is brick-red to tan with a paler margin and the flesh is mild rather than the intensely bitter taste of Sulphur Tuft.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Galerina marginata
dangerousLookalikes.note: DEADLY (amatoxins). Also clusters on dead wood but has a rusty-brown spore print (not purple-brown), a browner cap, and a more distinct membranous ring. Lethal if eaten.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Armillaria mellea
dangerousLookalikes.note: Honey fungus. Clusters on wood/roots but is honey-brown with a whitish spore print, a persistent ring, and fine dark scales on the cap; edible only when thoroughly cooked.
